answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to one endpoint that peers probe at random times. It must answer signed challenges, proving it is a live service, not a hollow shell registered in bulk. A shared host, copied setup, or identical timing marks the whole plume of lookalikes as suspect, and failures strip standing. Like a tide returning without warning, probes keep coming, so an attacker cannot wake thousands of dormant identities for one vote: each needs real hosting, upkeep, and prompt correct answers. Cheap copies sink; only maintained endpoints earn paid work.
